Replaced the `if y <= 0.25` block to always use Chebyshev series evaluation when `y > 0.0`, removing the `_XSML` threshold. The original port fell back to `1.0 / x` for tiny post-reduction values, which fails near π where precision cancellation produces `y ≈ 7.4e-11`. Using the series instead leverages the accurate Chebyshev expansion designed for small arguments, computing cot correctly even after modulo reduction to the fundamental domain. The fallback `1.0 / x` is now only used when `y = 0` exactly (avoids 0/0).
